assessments.reasoning: Section 4.4.4.1 adds the offset and address as integers, selects the 32-bit width when an instruction has no narrow width, and traps when effective address plus width in bytes exceeds memory data length.

challenge.method: Confirm the full i32 width in section 2.3.1 and independently try a one-page memory with nonzero static offset. Check exactly reaching the end, one byte beyond, and a large unsigned address that would appear in range if addition wrapped.
challenge.results: The exactly ending four-byte read succeeds. The one-byte overflow and would-wrap cases trap. The result is attached to the full-width Core 1.0 instruction and concerns that bounds failure, apart from host exception APIs.

limitations: The four-byte width is specific to full-width i32.load. Narrow loads have different widths. This addresses the bounds test, independent of host buffering and JavaScript API errors.
Exact dated publications govern the scope. The independently constructed current-engine cases are a supplementary challenge.
